method: tools/parity/oidc-differential.cjs against isolated copies of the API-initialized pinned v2.37.2 fixture and one ephemeral local RS256 provider; 22 Node-versus-Go cases include a successful web OIDC login followed by logout and cookie/session-state comparison.
normalization: JWT signatures and random token bytes are not retained; algorithms and claims are compared, normalizing only UUID-valued identifiers and timestamps. Each ID-token nonce is checked against the nonce from that same side authorization flow.
Node and Go use separate copied fixture directories and database files. Only fixture-specific backup paths are normalized in API settings; persisted user fields and session counts remain compared.

JSON object member order is canonicalized for Socket.IO payload comparison because JSON object order is not semantically significant; array order, scalar values, null versus empty, and linked-user raw persisted extraData text remain strict.
limits: Logout evidence covers one successful web OIDC session with no configured provider end-session URL. allDevices, missing/invalid refresh token, logout callback/provider errors, mobile logout, and broader cookie/session invalidation variants remain unverified.

preFixMismatch.replay: both return 400 No session; both preserve zero provider-linked users and sessions

differences: Go omitted Express weak ETag on res.json-equivalent logout body
Go did not re-emit the signed connect.sid session cookie
Go added Max-Age, HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite attributes absent from upstream clearCookie headers
preFixLogoutMismatch.persistedSessionEffect: Both implementations removed the one refresh session row.
